Harbour lights

Harbour lights came on an hour early on Tuesday, after the fog settled over the quay and the evening ferry waited outside the bar.

The harbour master said the delay was a tide, not a fault. Two cargo barges stayed at the outer buoy until the channel mark was visible again.

Shopkeepers along the front kept their doors open. The fish market closed its shutters and left a chalk note for the morning auction.

A pilot boat made three slow passes. Each pass checked the same red buoy, and each time the buoy was where the chart said it should be.

Passengers on the delayed ferry could see the town and could not yet reach it. The captain read the tide table twice and then once more over the radio.

By dusk the fog lifted from the inner basin first. The outer road stayed grey. The lights on the breakwater were the only sharp points in it.

The night watch wrote the times in a paper log. The guest that reads this page should keep these paragraphs and drop the cookie banner and the sidebar.

What the quay recorded

The first barge came in at 18:40. The second followed twelve minutes later. Neither needed a tug. The ferry took the inside berth.

Crates of apples and a pallet of machine parts were the only cargo listed. The parts were labelled for a workshop up the hill, not for the port itself.

A child on the quay counted the lamps. There are forty-two along the front and six more on the pier. Two of the pier lamps flicker and are due for repair in the spring.
